summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests exercise therapy, mainly walking, in men with localized prostate cancer who are on active surveillance. Participants do individualized walking, up to 5 sessions per week, for a total of 225 to 300 minutes per week, until their next standard prostate biopsy, which is about 6 to 12 months away. The study aims to measure effects on molecular, imaging, and pathology markers compared with usual care.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la terapia con ejercicio, principalmente caminar, en hombres con cáncer de próstata localizado que están en vigilancia activa. Los participantes hacen caminatas individualizadas, hasta 5 sesiones por semana, con un total de 225 a 300 minutos por semana, hasta su próxima biopsia de próstata estándar, que ocurre en unos 6 a 12 meses. El estudio busca medir los efectos sobre marcadores moleculares, radiológicos y patológicos en comparación con la atención habitual.
who_for: Histologically confirmed localized prostate cancer undergoing active surveillance.
Not meeting national exercise guidelines (under 150 minutes per week of moderate or vigorous exercise) based on 7-day tracking.
Cleared for exercise by exercise physiologist ECG review and the PAR-Q+ questionnaire.
not_for: Enrolled in another program that may alter exercise effects on tumor outcomes, such as a weight loss program.
Neoadjuvant anticancer treatment of any kind for prostate cancer in the last 5 years.
Systemic anticancer therapy in the last 15 years.
Distant metastatic malignancy of any kind.
Other condition or illness that the investigator judges makes the person a poor candidate.
